_comment: Correction-note evidence (S2): Llama-2-7B YaRN at the paper's actual
factors, measured twice so the anchor's contribution is separable.
For each (factor, context) the pair is mis-anchored vs correctly anchored.
The gate script writes the numbers (perplexity after a full-length prompt,
the generation's early-EOS/blank-line/repetition scores, and the effective
inv_freq it asserted from the built model). These are the evidence for the
correction note; they are NEVER reported as speculative-decoding results.
`expect` is deliberately absent: this is a measurement, and the gate's
pass/fail rule is not the point here. The claim under test is that the
anchor explains most of the perplexity damage and NOT the degeneration,
which is read off the numbers rather than off a verdict.

WHAT THE RATIOS MEASURE. Each candidate is scored against the unscaled model at the SAME context (32k or 128k), so a ratio isolates the effect of the ANCHORING CHOICE for a model that is already being shown an out-of-distribution context. It is not a quality comparison against an in-distribution model, and the unscaled 32k/128k rows are therefore labelled `unscaled_ood_reference`, not `native`. The one in-distribution measurement -- Llama-2 native at 4096 -- is included as `in_distribution_reference` and reported descriptively beside the others.

PAIRING. Each OOD reference row (`unscaled_ood_reference`) shares the seed of the candidates at its own context, so the anchored-vs-misanchored contrast is PAIRED: the same sample, scored twice, with only the rope's anchoring differing. The 4096 row is `in_distribution_reference` and is descriptive -- it is reported beside the ratios, never used as a denominator, and it is not paired with anything.

candidates.name: B_llama2_native_4096
candidates._what_it_is: Llama-2-7B at 4096, the length it was trained on, with its shipped rope. This IS the in-distribution reference, and it is here to be reported BESIDE the ratios rather than as their denominator: it answers 'what does this model's perplexity look like where it is valid', which the 32k and 128k denominators cannot answer because no anchoring choice makes the model in-distribution at those lengths.

candidates.name: B_llama2_unscaled_ood_32k
candidates._what_it_is: Llama-2-7B with its SHIPPED rope, shown a 32k context: the unscaled model at an out-of-distribution length. This is the denominator for the anchoring ratios and it is NOT a native reference -- 32k is four times the length the model was trained on. Labelling it 'native' would invite reading a ratio against it as quality relative to an in-distribution model, which is not what the number measures. Seed 42, the same seed the candidates at this context use, so the reference and the candidate score the SAME document, offset, prompt and continuation.

candidates.name: B_llama2_unscaled_ood_128k
candidates._what_it_is: The same unscaled reference at 128k: 32x the training window. Included so that every mis-anchored / correctly-anchored pair has a denominator measured at its OWN context. Seed 42, the same seed the candidates at this context use, so the reference and the candidate score the SAME document, offset, prompt and continuation.
